- Proposed cutover window: 2027-10-05 to 2027-10-07 (can narrow).
- Canary plan: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 rollouts, monitor token error rate and 95th latency.

What's in the sample:

- Example idempotency pattern for mutating calls (Idempotency-Key header).
- Config templates for timeouts and backoff.

Carla — thanks, good data. Pasted below is a compact guidance block (also in cutover-runbook.pdf attachment). I'll summarize then include an inline pseudo-code example.

Operational recommendations
- Timeouts: connect=2s, request/read=15s for typical calls; streaming endpoints use 45s read timeout with parallel heartbeat pings.
- Retries: 3 attempts max for idempotent calls (GETs, safe ops), exponential backoff with jitter: base=200ms, factor=2, max_backoff=8s.
- 429 handling: treat 429 as a signal to slow down — immediate backoff and increase client-side token bucket interval. Do not retry immediately without backoff.
- 503/502: eligible for retry with backoff (same policy as above). Persistent 5xx across >30s window -> trigger rollback.
- Idempotency: include Idempotency-Key for any operation that can result in duplicate effects.

Canary / cutover plan (detailed)
1) Sandbox validation (internal): run sample harness against staging endpoints for 48 hours.
2) Pre-cutover run: smoke test with 1000 requests/minute for 30m.
3) Canary 1 (5%): route 5% production traffic -> 30m steady-state -> validate metrics (error-rate < 0.5%, latency 95th < 600ms).
4) Canary 2 (25%): 1 hour -> validate and check billing/quotas.
5) Canary 3 (50%): 2 hours -> validate; if OK, schedule 100% for next maintenance window.
6) Rollback: flip routing to legacy endpoints and re-run step #2. Documented in cutover-runbook.pdf.

Sample pseudo-code (Node)
- show snippet inline (minimal):

const DEFAULT_BACKOFF = 200 // ms
function backoff(attempt) {
  const jitter = Math.random() * 100
  return Math.min(8000, DEFAULT_BACKOFF * Math.pow(2, attempt)) + jitter
}

async function resilientRequest(reqOptions) {
  let attempt = 0
  while (attempt < 3) {
    const res = await httpClient.request(reqOptions)
    if (res.status === 200) return res.body
    if (res.status === 429) {
      // signal: slow down; increase client token bucket interval
      await sleep(backoff(attempt))
      attempt++
      continue
    }
    if (res.status >= 500 && res.status < 600) {
      await sleep(backoff(attempt))
      attempt++
      continue
    }
    // other statuses: surface to caller
    throw new Error(`Unexpected status ${res.status}`)
  }
  throw new Error('RetryAttemptsExceeded')
}

Other small notes:
- Use X-Request-ID and Idempotency-Key headers for tracing and dedupe.
- Prefer batching short messages where possible: grouping 5 small prompts into a single request lowers unit cost and reduces rate-limit pressure.

Carla — adding a couple operational items from CS/ops side so the SREs have everything they need during the canary:

Observability & alerts- Dashboard seed: token-rate (per-route), 95th latency, error-rate-5xx, 429-rate, downstream-DB-latency.
- Alert thresholds: error-rate-5xx > 0.5% for 5m, 429-rate spike > 1% sustained for 10m.

Quota & throttle settings- We'll provision a soft quota for NimblePay during canary: 500 rps quota with burst bucket = 1000 for 2m. If you see sustained 429s, open a P0 to the integration channel and we can bump temporarily.

Support & escalation- On-call contact: integration-runbook Slack channel + Redwood SRE pager (redwood-sre-oncall@pager.example).
- Monica (CS) will own rollback coordination; Vivek will own infra-side kernel toggles for routing.

Next steps (action items)
1) Carla: confirm final canary start time (we tentatively hold 2027-10-05 00:00 UTC).
2) NimblePay: run the SDK sample in staging and post the telemetry link.
3) Redwood: provide DocuSign for the PO (Monica will cc Procurement).

Regards,
